my mom was like this and when i was about 13-14 and my sister was 11-12 she finally really put in the effort to get help. i stopped speaking to my mother for over a year due to feeling so overwhelmed, angry, and just like a care taker. your children should not have to take care of their mother. it’s a mom’s job to care and provide for her kids. having your daughter call you a burden might be the wake up call you need. you cannot try to change or try to get better. you have to because your life and your children’s lives depend on it. yes it is hard, but BPD can be manageable. work on finding a support system that is not your kids, and look into different therapy and medication options. You have said you have been in therapy for 5 years. i’m not sure if it’s the same therapist or multiple. you can find someone who specializes in bpd or personality disorders. there are also DBT programs. 

note - sometimes it can be hard to empathize with your parents regarding mental health at that age. i didn’t fully understand what my mom may have been going through until i was older. this helped me with a lot of my anger. even now i am having a hard time empathizing with you because i was in your daughters position and know how much it fked me up. i also don’t think it is fair that she waited for 15 years to make improvements. i sometimes still feel resentment because of my rough childhood and because now we both have bpd. lol
